bibl.title: Imaging Inscriptions: The Kingston Lacy Obelisk.
bibl.seg: Jane Masséglia, Imaging Inscriptions: The Kingston Lacy Obelisk.
Alan Bowman & Charles Crowther (edd.), The Epigraphy of Ptolemaic Egypt = Oxford Studies in Ancient Documents (Oxford, 2020) pp. 9-19, figg.
bibl.note: The granite obelisk with inscriptions in Hieroglyphic and Greek which was transported by W.J. Bankes from Philae in Egypt to his home at Kingston Lacy in Dorset in 1829 played an important role in the story of the decipherment of hieroglyphs by Young and Champollion. Coinciding with the launch of the Rosetta Spacecraft mission in 2014, new digital images of the inscriptions on the base of the obelisk were made by a team from the Centre for the Study of Ancient Documents, University of Oxford, using the technique of Reflectance Transformation Imaging (RTI) and allowed improved versions of the texts to be corrected and verified.
